properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/02/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8185763
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/02/2024
Comments: On 5/2/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling/completions inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 60 degrees and mostly clear when I arrived on location. When I arrived at the site, I met Seneca's Company man, Wesley Sammons who described current operations as follows: The Patterson 801 drilling rig is set up on site drilling production on four of five new wells. This rig arrived on site and started drilling on 3/31/2024. The crew was currently drilling the production section on the 75HU well and were in the process of drilling the curve, currently being at 11,444 feet. The lateral section will follow with the total depth expected to be 25,743 feet. After this well, there are two more to follow with this rig drilling just the production sections. The surface and intermediate sections were previously drilled by a different rig. Wes expects it to take until approximately 6/24/2024 for the rig to finish at the site.Wes accompanied me on the site inspection. The rig and ancillary equipment were stationed on secondary containment. Chemicals were staged on secondary containment. There were 10 frac tanks on the northeast side of the rig staged in secondary containment, these being used for various drilling fluids. There were two frac tanks on the southeast side of the rig that were used to store rainwater collected from the pad surface. This water was being used for drilling fluids. The drill cuttings were being solidified with a plant-based substance called slate dry and with wood pellets prior to being transported offsite to a waste disposal facility. I did witness drill cuttings being piled up above the level of the exterior wall of an open-top tank. I discussed keeping the level of the material low enough to allow for necessary free board. During a previous inspection I witnessed elevated conductance water along the north perimeter berm. I did not witness water in this area during this inspection. Following up on a previous inspection, I collected water sample 9551-108 from the sediment basin near the center overflow inlet box and water sample 9551109 from within the outlet pipe at the corresponding drain grate. No E and S issues were observed during the time of the inspection. Temporary compost filter socks have been installed throughout the construction site. Vegetation is becoming established in recently constructed areas but the requirements for permanent stabilization have not been met yet. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Infiltration berms 2 and 3 and the sedimentation basin do not yet meet the vegetative requirements for permanent stabilization.Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 and ID 3736567 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations. The DEP recommends the following: 1. Prevent water with elevated levels of aluminum from leaving the pad surface, from entering the sediment basin, from leaving the LOD and from infiltrating into the groundwater. 2. Continues the process of determining the source of contamination as witnessed in this and prior inspections. 3. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad and entering the sediment basin. Clean and report as necessary.4. Maintain adequate levels of freeboard in open-topped containers including the half-round dumpsters being used for drill cuttings.5. Continue to monitor the stability and functionality of the sediment traps and sediment basin and repair as necessary.I left the site at 1110 hours.

Comments: This inspection was to follow up with information that was provided to the Department concerning this well. The data provided did not meet expectations and led to more confusion so a notice of violation is being written. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/02/2020 to PVE OIL CORP INC in Sergeant Twp, McKean county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PVE OIL CORP INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/02/2020
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 900915
Permit API: 083-57192
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Sergeant Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/02/2020
Comments: The operator called the Department to report a spill at the Burning Well PV-81 well site on December 2nd at 9:20 am. The Complaint ID for this spill is #353829.A tree near the well fell due to heavy snow and wind overnight onto the lead line of the well, causing a union to fail. The well is pumped with an electric powered pumpjack that is on a timer. This well begins to pump at 8:00 am. At 8:30 am, the well pumper came by and found the well leaking. He immediately shut the well in and informed the operator of the spill. The tree was cut off the line and the flow of oil was stopped. Dave Hill plus two well pumpers from PVE were on site when I arrived, as were three representatives of Howard Drilling, who had been called to help clean the oil up. They were using a portable vacuum tank to collect any loose oil they could find. The oil appears to be caught in the snow in an area approximately 15-20 feet circular down gradient from the spot of the leak. No oil flowed outside this area, as heavy snow acted to slow and prevent seepage. It appears as though 10-20 gallons of crude oil was spilled from the compromised line. The operator has cleared the top of the tree from this area to begin cleanup. Snow and debris have been cleared at the edge of the contaminated area. The operator has placed a continuous pile of absorbent peat in this cleared area around the spill as a berm. They intend to rake and shovel the oily snow and debris to the center of the area, then load it into two or more plastic totes that will be used as temporary storage. The entire area will then be covered again with peat for the time being. When conditions allow, they intend to dig up any soil that is contaminated and haul it to the landfill, along with the oil covered sticks from the site. Continued inspection will be performed on this site as cleanup progresses. See attached sheet for violations.

Comments: On March 10, 2022, inspection conducted at the Master Splinter well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3486354, where it was noted that repairs and remediation appeared to have been performed in accordance with the operator's NOV response. The remediated areas were also noted to be establishing vegetation. The following was observed:The formerly impacted areas have established additional vegetation since the date of IR 3486354 (see photos 4 and 9). The Act 9 sign was present at the entrance of the access road and was not obscured by vegetation (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photos 2). The access road and well pad appeared to be stable at the time of inspection with no concerns related to accelerated erosion or vegetative coverage see photos 3 and 5). Well tags were present on the well heads with no observed leaks or discharge on ground around them (see photo 7). Production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment did not have any observable leaks (see photo 8). GPU units were equipped with secondary containment (see photo 6). Soil conductivities were taken in the formerly impacted areas, which were found to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil (see photos 10-12). Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remediation work has been completed. Closure of violations shall be contingent upon Act 2 approval and a subsequent CEI inspection.

Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC

Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 8266631
Permit API: 051-21886
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/02/2026
Comments: On March 2, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4128962.The Department and the Operator entered into a COA for this site in March 7, 2019.E and S Plans on-site are not updated as discussed in IR 4128962. The Department requested new E and S phase and Restoration phase drawings added to the plan set to include the rough delineation of the wetland. The Department also requested adding a wetland seed mix to the delineated wetland, which has also not been added to the plan set. CFS near the access road entrance and stockpile along the access road appear to have been impacted by truck traffic. The Department recommends the operator maintain the CFS and ensure it is installed properly. No E and S issues are observed at this time.Orange construction fence has been installed surrounding the flowing surface water from the wetland. Operator has added compost chinking to the existing CFS on-site. No additional CFS appears to have been installed at this time. CFS surrounding the site and wetland appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. No E and S issues are observed at this time. What appears to be absorbent pads are observed within the flowing water on site (Photos 14-16, 22). Specific conductivity was recorded for background and within the area of the absorbent pads to assess for possible spill. The Department did not observe elevated specific conductivity readings or a sheen in the water near the pads. However the Department requests a response with information on why the absorbent pads are located within the water on site.The pipe identified in IRs 4125575 and 4128962 appears to have been removed as described by the operator in the NOV response. As requested in IR 4128962, the Department requests a written response to include any findings regarding the pipe, including the size of the pipe, use, and if it was connected to additional equipment. Violations remain outstanding at this time. The Department requests the plan set be updated and a written response be received by the Department by March 16, 2026.

There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PETRO ERIE INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/21/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8156112
Permit API: 121-44463
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/21/2023
Comments: Onsite for a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3602052 dated 8/17/2023. The previous inspection report references a black plastic brine line, (2) brine tanks, and a separate tank battery with (4) steel tanks.There is a 100bbl fiberglass tank and a 100bbl poly tank onsite that appears to be the brine storage tanks for the well. The two tanks are plumbed together with piping and valves open to equalize the fluid in each tank. There does not appear to be a way to empty either tank by means of a water truck hose connection without altering the plumbing of the tanks. However, the 2" black poly line that runs from the hillside from the wells on the lease and ties into the brine tanks has a "T" fitting and a valve to discharge produced fluid to the ground via a ditch from a cross-culvert of the access road.The 2" valve on the black poly pipeline is closed and plugged. The pipe was not actively discharging or leaking. However, there is a visible impact area within the ditch of the cross-culvert and which the black poly line is laid. Soil conductivity readings indicate that a brine discharge has occurred at the site. The impacted area inside the ditch extends approximately 80' downslope from the access road culvert and ending just before a second culvert for another old access road. The width on average of the ditch is about 5'. The amount of the discharged produced fluid is unknown.Violations are cited.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Pa Gen Energy Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-01-30
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 840719
Permit API: 105-21651
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Wharton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-01-30
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of PGE's Pine Hill 1941 Well Pad in Wharton Twp, Potter County on 1/30/2019 at 1215 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a spill reported to the DEP Report hotline by Nathan Harris (PGE). It was reported that at approximately 0900 a vac truck that was moving produced water from a production tank had "collapsed". The tank was estimated to have had 25 barrels of liquid inside when it collapsed. DEP WQS, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived onsite at 1215 hours. When we arrived the truck was still in place and crew was observed sucking up fluids from the pad surface. We observed the vac truck(see photo #1) and the impacted area (photo #2 & 14). Puddles and slush mixes were field measured with a PCSTestr returning readings ranging from ~2.0 ms/cm to ~15.0 ms/cm (see photos #3, 4 & 5). We spoke with Erick Duzick (PGE Completions Engineer) onsite who explained the vac trucks relief valve was frozen solid which had caused the truck to create a vacuum which in return caused the vac truck tank to implode. The truck driver reported that liquid was released from the back hatch and from a small hole in the side of the tank (see photos #10 &11). It appeared that most of the liquid would have released from the back hatch. The truck driver also mentioned that by the time he got a ride and another vac truck onsite, approximately 1.5 hours had passed before clean-up was underway. He also estimated (using the site glass) that ~25 barrels were in the truck before it imploded. The other vac truck driver that was onsite for clean-up explained to us that when he dropped off the recovered liquids at Clermont Storage Facility that he could let us know how much was recovered from the pad surface. Crew began scraping pad material when we were onsite. See photos #8, 9, & 12 showing the excavator and pile of impacted pad material/snow recovered. The material was then temporarily transferred to a sheet of plastic until a roll-off truck could make it onsite. A wrecker was also on the way to transport the vac truck. Observations made in the field confirmed that the release was more than 42 gallons. The operator should refer to the procedures outlined in 25 Pa Code Section 78a66(c)(2) pertaining to remediating releases greater than 42 gallons. Sample 0935-404 was collected by Jonathan approximately 10 feet north of the containment surrounding the production tanks. This sample was a snow mix from the pile of excavated material and will be submitted for metals only. We departed the site at 1330 hours. Due to observations made during the course of the inspection violations of the following are cited against Well Permit API #105-21651: 35 P.S. Section 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 Operator called on 1/31/2019 and reported that the clean-up was completed and screening of the impacted area was completed. Inspection Date: 2019-01-30
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of PGE's Pine Hill 1941 Well Pad in Wharton Twp, Potter County on 1/30/2019 at 1215 hours. The inspection was conducted in response to a spill reported to the DEP Report hotline by Nathan Harris (PGE). It was reported that at approximately 0900 a vac truck that was moving produced water from a production tank had "collapsed". The tank was estimated to have had 25 barrels of liquid inside when it collapsed. DEP WQS, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived onsite at 1215 hours. When we arrived the truck was still in place and crew was observed sucking up fluids from the pad surface. We observed the vac truck(see photo #1) and the impacted area (photo #2 & 14). Puddles and slush mixes were field measured with a PCSTestr returning readings ranging from ~2.0 ms/cm to ~15.0 ms/cm (see photos #3, 4 & 5). We spoke with Erick Duzick (PGE Completions Engineer) onsite who explained the vac trucks relief valve was frozen solid which had caused the truck to create a vacuum which in return caused the vac truck tank to implode. The truck driver reported that liquid was released from the back hatch and from a small hole in the side of the tank (see photos #10 &11). It appeared that most of the liquid would have released from the back hatch. The truck driver also mentioned that by the time he got a ride and another vac truck onsite, approximately 1.5 hours had passed before clean-up was underway. He also estimated (using the site glass) that ~25 barrels were in the truck before it imploded. The other vac truck driver that was onsite for clean-up explained to us that when he dropped off the recovered liquids at Clermont Storage Facility that he could let us know how much was recovered from the pad surface. Crew began scraping pad material when we were onsite. See photos #8, 9, & 12 showing the excavator and pile of impacted pad material/snow recovered. The material was then temporarily transferred to a sheet of plastic until a roll-off truck could make it onsite. A wrecker was also on the way to transport the vac truck. Observations made in the field confirmed that the release was more than 42 gallons. The operator should refer to the procedures outlined in 25 Pa Code Section 78a66(c)(2) pertaining to remediating releases greater than 42 gallons. Sample 0935-404 was collected by Jonathan approximately 10 feet north of the containment surrounding the production tanks. This sample was a snow mix from the pile of excavated material and will be submitted for metals only. We departed the site at 1330 hours. Due to observations made during the course of the inspection violations of the following are cited against Well Permit API #105-21651: 35 P.S. Section 691.402(b) 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.57(a) 35 P.S. Section 6018.301 Operator called on 1/31/2019 and reported that the clean-up was completed and screening of the impacted area was completed. Violations will remain open until remediation and reporting is conducted in compliance with 25 Pa. Code Section 78a.66.

Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection (FUI) on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.On a FUI on 8/19/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3816085), I noted the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. I emailed Ray Hepler information about Act 2 remediation. On 8/28/2024, Jack Crow, Henry Kramer, Brian Shank and myself met with Ray Hepler at the PA DEP Meadville Regional Office to discuss the outstanding violations at the Wheeler property. Ray Hepler stated he had the contaminated soil from the brine releases on a roll off and would send us the manifests soon. The Department received a manifest for waste on 9/9/2024. However, the manifest stated the soil was "Beaver-PA 100%". The manifest also stated the soil was hauled in a "white pick up truck", but during the 8/28/2024 meeting Ray Hepler stated the soil was in a roll off container. This manifest does not show the proper disposal of the soil from the Wheeler W12 well site located in Jefferson County. Today (9/12/2024), Brian Shank and I conducted a FUI. The pipe not necessary for production was still being stored near the access road. The spill area appeared to have new top soil and grass seed. We collected soil conductivity readings throughout the spill area. A background soil conductivity reading was collected. The soil conductivity reading was 154.5 pS/cm. Near the production tank, the soil conductivity reading was 3.28 mS/cm. Approximately 4 feet from the production tank, the soil conductivity reading 1416 pS/cm. These readings indicate that the prior spill has not been remediated yet. We collected grab soil samples to send to the Department's accredited laboratory. The samples will be analyzed for SAC 960 and UVIR.The outstanding violations for the Wheeler W12 well site will remain open at this time.

Comments: On April 30, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resource's Drape James Well Pad (ESCGP-3 issued: 3/29/23 and expires: 3/28/28) located in Frazer Township, Allegheny County in response to CTS #380249.Nick Reda of Range Resources reportedly noticed on April 30, 2024 at 8:15AM an approximately 84 gallon release of water based drill mud on the graveled well pad in several areas. Nick notified the emergency hotline by 10:02AM and believes there is likely one or more holes in the secondary containment causing fluid to leech out from under the containment.The findings of this inspection are as follows: Upon walking the well pad, orange spray paint markings were made by Nick to designate the affected areas plus some buffer space since it was starting to rain. 7 distinct designated areas were observed, some areas had puddles of fluid in them while other areas had stained gravel. Some puddles were cloudy while others appeared to have a sheen to them. Pooling of fluid with sheen were also seen on the secondary containment in some areas.Conductivity readings were taken inside the different spill areas as well as adjacent to the marked spill areas to determine whether any areas outside of these markings were contaminated as well. A background conductivity reading was taken at the well pad perimeter upslope (0.0159 mS) and the rest of the readings are as follows: inside Spill Area 1: 12.6 mS, outside of Spill Area 1: 0.085 mS, inside of Spill Area 3: 1.529 mS, inside of Spill Area 4: 2.05 mS, outside of Spill Area 4: 0.011 mS, from in a cloudy puddle seen in Spill Area 5: Over Range, outside of Spill Area 5: 0.011 mS, inside Spill Area 6: 1.762 mS, from a sheen puddle seen in Spill Area 7: Over range, and lastly 3 readings were taken in stained sediment around the well pad to see if there were other contaminated areas: 0.042 mS, 0.693 mS and 0.0227 mS. These readings subjugate that a release has in fact occurred, that the areas marked by Nick are the contaminated areas, and that at the time of the inspection the release had not appeared to seep past the visibly marked contaminated areas. The perimeter of the well site on the side of the pad where the release occurred was walked and 2 key way drains were investigated. Both drains were dry and soil conductivity readings were taken at each one (0.091 mS and 0.027 mS). Based on these conductivity readings and the lack of fluid coming from the drains, it does not appear that at this time, the release has seeped down into the drainage system.While onsite, SPSI arrived to begin the remediation process. A skid steer was observed scraping up contaminated gravel into piles, a vacuum truck and 2 clamshell roll off dumpsters were scheduled to arrive today and once they do, the truck will suck up all contaminated fluids and the skid steer will pick up all reachable contaminated gravel/sediment and place it in the dumpsters for disposal. Nick stated that Range was not sure on an exact area in which the release originated from. In theory, Range believes there to be one or more holes/tears in the secondary containment, but none of them have reportedly been discovered at the time of the inspection. Nick stated that the drill rig has two more weeks on site. During these two weeks as equipment is removed and once the drill rig is gone, Range plans to continue inspecting the secondary containment, specifically in areas that currently have equipment on top of it. Any further releases will continue to be cleaned and any holes/tears will be repaired as they are found. The Department recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release and promptly find and repair any holes or tears in the secondary containment to prevent any further releases. The Department also requests the Operator notify the Department of any further releases or impacts that occur and supply the Department with secondary containment inspection reports within 2 business days of receipt of this report.

Comments: This inspection occurred in response to a phone called made by Jeff Passarello, of Seneca Resources, to Alexis Jacobs, WQS with the Department, on April 20th, 2026. The purpose of the phone call was to report an incident which had occurred on the E08-T well pad.It was reported that approximately 1 barrel of production fluid was released from a maintenance failure on a pump used to support the transport of production fluid through a pipeline. The failure was immediately addressed and corrected to stop the production fluid from leaving the pipeline. The pump was in secondary containment, although a majority of the production fluid discharged outside of the containment onto the well pad and onto the fill material beyond the well pad. Upon arrival to the site, a skid steer was being used to remove contaminated material from the well pad. One dumpster was on site which contained the contaminated waste from the incident. A second dumpster was being transported to the site at the time of this inspection. The released production fluid appeared to be primarily within 10 yards of where the incident occurred on the well pad. A mini excavator was used to scrape approximately an inch of surface material from the pad where the spill occurred. This material was in a pile to be removed from the pad and placed into a dumpster for disposal. The impacted soils beyond the edge of the well pad were also excavated and placed into a dumpster for disposal. The excavated area beyond the pad was approximately 10 yards x 5 yards. Evidence of production fluid did not appear to be present beyond the excavated area. A copy of the disposal slip from the landfill is expected to be provided to the Department when available.Confirmatory field sampling will need to occur to confirm full remediation of the site. The Department's Policy 800-5000-001- "Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil and Gas Well Sites or Access Roads" sets forth the procedure to be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release documented in this Notice of Violation ("NOV"), by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. Follow up inspections will be performed routinely until the cleanup is deemed complete.

Comments: On July 28, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Cowden 6H gas well located on the Cowden 16 well pad in Hopewell Twp, Washington County following IR 4139756, where violations were issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) on site and failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad.Big Dog Energy (BDE) is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 16 well pad, however, according to DEP records, Diversified owns both the gas wells on the pad and the well pad. Violations issued for failure to have an ERP on site are being continued at this time.A graveled access road was observed to lead to the Cowden 16 gas well pad. (Photo 4).3 gas wells and 1 plugged gas well monument was observed on the Cowden 16 well pad. The 6H gas wellhead had a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the 6H gas wellhead at the time of this inspection. (Photos 5-6)A white storage tank was still observed to be on the Cowden 16 gas well pad and not connected for production (Photos 7-9). Therefore, violations issued for failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) are being continued at this time.An area on the left side of the gas well pad was observed to have dying vegetation. Mr. Scott stated that roundup weed killer was applied to this section of the gas well pad (Photos 10-11). Based on today's inspection, violations issued for failure to have an Emergency Response Plan on site and failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad are being continued for the 6H gas well at this time.

Inspection Date: 12/01/2022
Comments: On December 1, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an administrative inspection for the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. Elevated levels of chloride and barium were found in the soil sample collected from the well pad surface. The results indicate that an unknown volume of produced fluid was spilled outside of containment to the well pad surface. The DEP received the Notice of Violation response from STL Resources on November 25, 2022 after approval of a response extension. STL Resources plans to remediate this spill in accordance to Chapter 78a.66. Based on the results from Soil Sample 0651-139 collected on October 24, 2022, additional violations of Chapter 78a.56(a), Solid Waste Management Section 301, and Chapter 78a.66(b)ii are being issued.

Comments: Based on the review of the well construction for the Thomas Greaves 6H well, the Department determined that the well was not drilled and cased in conformance casing and cementing requirements in the 2012 Oil and Gas Act (58 Pa. C.S. §§ 3201-3274) and 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78. The operator failed to segregate and protect the workable Pittsburgh coal seam by setting and cementing a coal protective casing across the workable Pittsburgh coal seam. The workable Pittsburgh coal seam was encountered from 670'-680'. Surface casing (20") is set at 376' and cemented to the surface. Coal protective casing (13 3/8") is set at 563' and cemented to surface. The coal protective casing is set 107' short of the Pittsburgh coal seam. Intermediate casing (9 5/8") is set at 1815'.
